lessons.title: Lesson 1 - Look, listen and repeat; Point and say; Let's talk

sentencePatterns.example: What's your address? - It's 75 Hoa Binh Lane.

languageSkills: Listening and reading street address vocabulary

languageKnowledge: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to ask and answer about addresses using 'What's your address? - It's...'
Pupils can correctly pronounce and use vocabulary: address, lane, street, avenue, flat.
languageSkills: Listen and understand conversations about personal addresses.
Ask and answer questions about personal addresses fluently.
generalCompetences: Autonomy and self-learning: Pupils prepare personal notes about their living area.
Communication and cooperation: Pupils interview partners in class politely.
qualities: Show responsibility and safety awareness regarding personal address information.

teacherActivities: Greet the class warmly ('Good morning/afternoon class! How are you today?').
Show pictures of different living environments (lane, street, tower, flat) on smartboard.
Ask pupils: 'Where do you live?' to activate background knowledge about address.
pupilActivities: Greet teacher warmly ('Good morning/afternoon teacher!').
Observe pictures attentively and call out familiar words in Vietnamese or English.
Share where they live with class and seatmates.
expectedOutcomes: 100% of pupils are engaged, motivated, and mentally ready for the lesson.
Pupils successfully activate background knowledge about addresses.

teacherActivities: [LANGUAGE FOCUS]: Present target vocabulary: "address" (/əˈdres/), "lane" (/leɪn/), "street" (/striːt/), "avenue" (/ˈæv.ə.njuː/), "flat" (/flæt/) with flashcards and clear pronunciation.
[LANGUAGE TARGET / PATTERNS]: Elicit target sentence structure: "What's your address? - It's [75 Hoa Binh Lane]". Model natural intonation.
Play audio track for Activity 1 (Look, listen and repeat). Pause for choral, row, and individual repetition.
Check pupil pronunciation and correct stress errors.
pupilActivities: Listen to audio track and repeat vocabulary: "address", "lane", "street", "avenue", "flat" in chorus and individually.
Track dialogue in textbook while listening.
Repeat sentence structure: "What's your address? - It's..." with partner.
expectedOutcomes: 85%+ of pupils correctly pronounce target address vocabulary with clear stress.
Pupils understand sentence structure "What's your address? - It's..."
Evidence of Integration [Digital Competence - DIG-PRIM-01]: Pupils practice repeating target audio with interactive digital audio player.

teacherActivities: [PRACTICE WITH LANGUAGE FOCUS]: Guide Activity 2 (Point and say) with prompts: 75 Hoa Binh Lane, 81 Tran Hung Dao Street, 12 Green Avenue, Flat 5 on second floor.
[APPLICATION WITH LANGUAGE TARGET]: Organize 'Classroom Address Interview' game: Pupils move around and ask partners: "What's your address? - It's..."
Monitor pairs, offer feedback, and encourage polite communication.
Invite 3-4 pupil pairs to demonstrate dialogue in front of class.
pupilActivities: Point to textbook picture prompts and practice saying address sentences with partners.
Role-play asking and answering classmates' addresses in pairwork.
Demonstrate dialogue in front of class with confidence.
expectedOutcomes: 90%+ of pupils fluently communicate addresses using target structure.
Pupils demonstrate active collaboration and polite communication in pairwork.
Evidence of Integration [Ethics - ETH-PRIM-01]: Pupils practice polite greeting and respectful listening during interview game.

teacherActivities: Summarize target vocabulary ("address", "lane", "street", "avenue", "flat") and structure ("What's your address?").
Integrate Safety & Privacy: Remind pupils to only share personal address with trusted people.
Assign workbook page 6 and home practice task.
pupilActivities: Recap address words and sentence patterns together with teacher.
Note down homework assignment and say 'Goodbye teacher!'.
expectedOutcomes: Pupils remember key language focus and sentence patterns.
Orderly lesson conclusion with privacy awareness.
Evidence of Integration [Digital Safety - NLS 4.2.CB1b]: Pupils demonstrate awareness of protecting personal address privacy.

integrationCandidates.title: Digital Audio Pronunciation Practice
integrationCandidates.description: Practicing address vocabulary using digital audio tracks.
suggestedActivities: Pupils listen and repeat with interactive audio track.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 - Look, listen and repeat; Point and say; Let's talk

sentencePatterns.example: What's your hometown like? - It's big and busy.

sentencePatterns.pattern: Where do you live? - I live in [Place].
sentencePatterns.example: Where do you live? - I live in a quiet village.

languageKnowledge: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to ask and describe what a place/hometown is like using 'What's your hometown like? - It's...'
Pupils master vocabulary describing places: hometown, city, mountain, village, tower, quiet, busy, large, pretty.
languageSkills: Listen to descriptions of hometowns and living places.
Speak about their own hometown with appropriate adjectives.
generalCompetences: Autonomy: Pupils reflect on their hometown scenery and characteristics.
Communication: Collaborate in pairs to exchange hometown descriptions.
qualities: Love for homeland and environmental awareness of local surroundings.

teacherActivities: Greet the class warmly.
Show pictures of different hometowns in Vietnam (mountains, coastal cities, quiet villages) on smartboard.
Play a short guessing game: 'Which hometown is this?'
pupilActivities: Greet teacher enthusiastically.
Guess the places from picture clues.
Share the name of their hometown with seatmates.
expectedOutcomes: 100% pupil engagement and interest excited.
Background knowledge about hometown descriptions activated.

teacherActivities: [LANGUAGE FOCUS]: Present new words: "hometown" (/ˈhəʊm.taʊn/), "city" (/ˈsɪt.i/), "mountain" (/ˈmaʊn.tɪn/), "village" (/ˈvɪl.ɪdʒ/), "tower" (/ˈtaʊ.ər/) with flashcards and stress modeling.
[LANGUAGE TARGET / PATTERNS]: Elicit target structure: "What's your hometown like? - It's [big and busy / quiet and small]". Model intonation.
Play audio for Activity 1 (Look, listen and repeat). Pause for repetition.
Check stress and pronunciation of Wh-questions.
pupilActivities: Listen to audio and repeat words and sentences in chorus and individually.
Read dialogue in pairs focusing on stress and intonation.
Practice asking and answering with target structure.
expectedOutcomes: 85%+ of pupils pronounce target hometown vocabulary accurately.
Pupils master sentence structure "What's your hometown like? - It's..."
Evidence of Integration [AI Literacy - AIL-PRIM-02]: Pupils use AI smart assistant to practice speaking hometown sentences.

teacherActivities: [PRACTICE WITH LANGUAGE FOCUS]: Guide Activity 2 (Point and say) with prompts: a. mountain / quiet, b. city / big and busy, c. village / small and pretty, d. tower / high and modern.
[APPLICATION WITH LANGUAGE TARGET]: Organize 'Hometown Reporter' game for Activity 3 (Let's talk): One pupil acts as a TV reporter asking classmates: "What's your hometown like? - It's..."
Monitor pairs, offer constructive feedback, and encourage active participation.
Invite 3 pupil reporter pairs to present dialogue.
pupilActivities: Practice pointing and saying with partners.
Role-play as reporter and interviewee asking and answering about hometowns.
Demonstrate dialogue in front of class with confidence.
expectedOutcomes: 90%+ of pupils describe hometowns fluently using target adjectives.
Active collaborative pairwork with high confidence.
Evidence of Integration [Environmental Education - ENV-PRIM-01]: Pupils connect hometown descriptions with keeping local nature clean.

teacherActivities: Summarize hometown vocabulary and target structure.
Integrate Environmental Protection: Remind pupils to keep their hometown clean and beautiful.
Assign workbook page 7.
pupilActivities: Recap target words with teacher.
Take notes on homework assignment in notebooks.
expectedOutcomes: Lesson content consolidated.
Environmental protection message reinforced.
Evidence of Integration [Environmental Education]: Hometown environmental awareness message established.
